bounded_statement: The selected result (exact two-sided Mann-Whitney U on 12 leaf records, U = 35.0, p = 0.004329) enters each of the six independent units (plants, per plant_id) twice into a rank-sum procedure whose exact null distribution treats every entered value as an independent observation; the reported significance at p < 0.01 is attributable to this repeated entry, since an exact Mann-Whitney test at the authorized plant level (3 vs 3 plant means, which show perfect group separation) cannot yield a two-sided p below 0.1.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses that leaf records were entered as individual observations and reports the true number of plants (3 per group) alongside the leaf-record count in the group summary table, so the unit inflation is not concealed; however, disclosure does not make the row-independent procedure valid for correlated within-plant rows.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: table reports 'leaf records' = 6 and 'plants' = 3 per group

evidence.description: The two leaf readings from each plant are tightly clustered relative to between-plant spread (e.g., PL-01: 96.2 and 99.8; PL-06: 179.4 and 186.0), showing within-plant dependence, so the two rows per plant are not independent draws and their repeated entry genuinely inflates evidence. Aggregating to plant means gives control plants 98.0, 115.15, 132.3 vs biochar plants 135.95, 160.95, 182.7; a 3-vs-3 exact two-sided Mann-Whitney test on these has minimum attainable p = 2/C(6,3) = 0.1, so the reported p < 0.01 cannot be reproduced at the independent-unit level.
evidence.observed_value: plant-level exact two-sided p = 0.1 (minimum possible for 3 vs 3) vs reported 0.004329

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the finding three ways. (1) Alternative independent unit: could leaves be the independent unit? No — data-description.md explicitly names plant_id as the independent-unit column, and treatment (amendment) is assigned at the pot/plant level in a single run, so leaves within a plant share both treatment assignment and plant-level variation; the data confirm within-plant clustering (paired leaf readings differ by 3.6–8.7 units while between-plant spread within groups is ~34–47 units). (2) Robustness of the conclusion: I recomputed the test at the plant level. Plant means are 98.0, 115.15, 132.3 (control) vs 135.95, 160.95, 182.7 (biochar); with perfect separation the exact two-sided Mann-Whitney p for 3 vs 3 is 2/20 = 0.1, the minimum attainable, so the reported p = 0.004329 and any claim of significance at conventional thresholds cannot be reproduced without the repeated per-plant entries. (3) Arithmetic check: 4/C(12,6) = 4/924 = 0.004329, exactly matching the reported p, confirming the test was run on 12 rows (6 vs 6), not 6 plants. All three checks confirm rather than falsify the issue.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py pools all leaf-level rows per amendment group in collect_groups (appending record conductance keyed only by amendment) and passes these pooled lists of 6 leaf values per group directly to scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu with method="exact", so each plant's two correlated leaf readings are counted as two independent observations, inflating the effective sample size from 3 vs 3 plants to 6 vs 6 rows and deflating the exact p-value from a minimum attainable 0.1 to 0.004329.
